title: Complete browser consent with the observed OpenAI callback and strict Origin validation
steps: Run the real OAuth authorize route with the OpenAI Portal callback, content scope, resource and S256 challenge while signed out.
Repeat with callback lookalikes and the obsolete private callback.

Submit Allow and Cancel in Chromium using the real signed consent page; inspect the browser-generated Origin and the real OAuth route response. Navigate to an intercepted foreign fixture to check referrer privacy; replay signed POSTs with null and foreign Origins.
expect: The valid request redirects to sign-in and preserves its exact callback and resource without minting a session.
Every invalid callback returns 400 invalid_request without a redirect.

Both browser submissions carry the exact Tracy Origin and return the expected 303 callback. Allow stores one site-bound code, Cancel stores none. No referrer reaches the foreign fixture; null and foreign Origins remain 403 without additional codes.
fence: Only the exact registered OpenAI callback can pass authorization validation; a signed-out request cannot read accounts or sites. Consent form navigation preserves the same-origin CSRF proof without disclosing a referrer across origins.

tests: OpenAI Portal callback reaches sign-in instead of invalid_request
OpenAI callback lookalikes and the obsolete callback are refused without redirect
browser consent allow: same-origin POST passes the strict Origin check without leaking a referrer
browser consent deny: same-origin POST passes the strict Origin check without leaking a referrer
